findings.summary: ADR honesty sentence for the attestation's trust envelope. I EXECUTED the escalated forgery at tip: `bd update <bead> --metadata '{"mindspec_stage_marker_oid":"<forged-tip>"}'` (one agent-runnable command; this bd version's merge semantics even preserve the other keys) + the same forged marker ref → the discriminator honored the resume, every gate was skipped, and the unowned file merged to the spec branch. This does NOT reopen F1: my round-1 fix direction (option (a)) explicitly modeled the spec-127 landed-merge pattern, which has the identical property; bd metadata is already the load-bearing store for landed-merge evidence and mindspec_phase, so a metadata-writing forger already had equivalent-power attacks pre-existing on main; the forgery now requires naming a source-known magic key in a deliberate bd write (unreachable by accident) and is inspection-detectable in Dolt history. But ADR-0041's new marker-provenance paragraph says the ATTESTED publication "proves" the gates passed, while the SAME document's re-attest amendment models the right convention ("detectable-by-inspection, NOT cryptographically tamper-proof, and this amendment claims exactly that and no more", ADR-0041 line ~628). Ask: add one equivalent sentence to the marker-provenance amendment (and optionally the stageMarkerAttestationKey doc comment's "binary-side publication evidence" phrasing) naming the bd-write-surface residual, so the ADR claims exactly what the mechanism provides. Doc-only, non-blocking.

POSITIVE — attestation design withstood the adversarial angles beyond the executed ones: cross-bead attestation reuse impossible (per-bead key, exact-OID compare); stale-attestation replay after completion cannot smuggle NEW content (a new commit moves the tip to neither the attested OID nor a commit whose child the marker is — and the unfinished-advance leg checks attestation BEFORE AdvanceBranchExpectedOld, so a forged marker cannot pull the branch ref); the attestation-write-before-ref-publish crash window is benign as documented (attestation without ref is inert; next publication overwrites); a TOCTOU racer needs the same bd write surface as the direct forgery, gaining nothing. The pre-fix in-flight-marker disclosure (FOREIGN once post-upgrade, one extra fully-gated run) is the safe direction of the migration.

POSITIVE — G2 empirically clean at tip: with stored=review present and both `bd list --parent` reads failing (logged shim), `state show` emitted clean stored-trusted output with no consistency warning and no fabricated derived phase — the exact scenario that pre-fix asserted `child-derived phase "plan"` from a failed read. Full-outage AC-1(ii) behavior unaffected (verified round 1).

Non-finding observations for the record: (1) this bd (1.1.0) MERGES `bd update --metadata` rather than replacing — code comments citing replace semantics (e.g. derive.go's Req 19/HC-5 rationale for never emitting raw `bd update` metadata recovery commands) are directionally stale but the guidance they justify remains correct, so nothing to change; (2) probe environment as in round 1: bd refuses temp-dir workspaces, so fixtures ran under a $HOME scratch dir, fully deleted; both checkouts verified byte-identical at 0783a507 (only the panel dir untracked); (3) mid-session harness classifier outages delayed some probes — all probes eventually executed, none skipped.
